newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA AND ATLETICO WARM UP FOR CUP CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA AND ATLETICO WARM UP FOR CUP CLASH.

text.p: Atletico Madrid and Barcelona have hit their best form leading up to their eagerly awaited Spanish Cup quarter-final on Wednesday.
The first leg will be the third game of 10 in a 35-day marathon for both teams which should prove decisive in their league, cup and European aspirations.

Barcelona fans remember all too well what happened last season when the two sides met in similar circumstances. Their team saw all three bids blow up in a disastrous 10 days which brought down coach Johan Cruyff.
Bayern Munich knocked Barca out of Europe but it was Atletico who killed off the Catalan club's hopes in both domestic league and cup.
Atletico won the cup final 1-0 and then the league fixture 3-1 in a memorable game.
Fans have become accustomed to seeing classic encounters between the two sides and the tradition continued earlier this season with an epic 3-3 league draw.

"The games seem to produce a lot of goals. Let's hope it's like that in favour of Barcelona," said Abelardo Fernandez, who celebrated his return to the Barcelona defence with a fine headed goal in Sunday's 4-1 win over Zaragoza.
Barcelona's three other goals were scored by Ronaldo, who put in one of his best performances of the season to silence those who had criticised him for going on holiday to the Rio carnival.
"Playing like that we'll win everything," he said.
But the striker left Spain immediately after the match and will miss Wednesday's game along with compatriot Giovanni through international duty.
Their absence could open the way to strikers Juan Pizzi, Angel Cuellar and midfielder Ivan de la Pena.
Troubled Bulgarian forward Hristo Stoichkov is another possible starter after a fine performance when he came on as substitute on Sunday.
Barring the way to the semifinal are an Atletico Madrid team once again showing some of the form which won the club their first league and cup double last season.

Atletico swept aside struggling Hercules 2-0 over the weekend using a first-choice line-up which surprised many commentators who felt that coach Radomir Antic had given up the league title to concentrate on the knock-out competitions.
Atletico seemed to have taken new heart from upsets which hit Barcelona and league leaders Real Madrid last week.

Although they are still 13 points adrift of Real, Antic's side have a game in hand and still have a very real chance of closing the seven-point gap on Barcelona to secure Spain's second European Cup place.
Just last week Betis looked the only likely rivals to Real Madrid and Barcelona for a place in Europe's most lucrative club competition.
But Betis have eked out only two points from the last nine at stake, while both Atletico and Deportivo Coruna have taken seven.
Deportivo beat Betis 3-0 on Sunday and joined them on 47 points, 12 off the pace.
The game brought comparisons with the 'Super-Depo' team which shook up the Spanish football hierarchy with the arrival of Brazilian striker Bebeto in 1992.
Bebeto's replacement in the hearts of the Deportivo faithful, Rivaldo, scored twice and is clearly blossoming under new coach and compatriot, Carlos Alberto Silva.
Yet another Brazilian, World Cup defender Mauro Silva, laughed when asked about his side's title hopes before replying realistically: "Second place is still within our reach."
